title: Networking: Terraform module for private VPC with endpoints & routing
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Create a reusable, production-grade Terraform module to provision private VPC networking for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support multi-AZ subnets (public/private/isolated), configurable NAT/IGW topology, optional centralized NAT vs per-AZ NAT gateways, VPC endpoints for core AWS services (S3, ECR, STS, CloudWatch Logs, Secrets Manager), and route table automation. This module will be the recommended baseline for customer VPCs for the Private product (VPC and on-prem variants).

Goals:
- Provide a single, well-documented module that operators and customers can consume with minimal overrides.
- Support safe upgrades and state migrations between module versions.
- Emit outputs required by other modules (bastion, k8s, load balancers, firewall) without leaking implementation details.
- Include built-in health-checking and a lightweight post-provisioning validator (Terraform null_resource + script) to validate routes, endpoints, and NAT reachability.

Non-goals:
- Implement provider-specific runtime autoscaling for NATs (handled by Dedicated infra in future).
- Replace customer's existing network design where strict customization is required; we provide extension hooks and well-documented overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Module can create a VPC with X public and Y private subnets across N AZs when invoked with minimal variables
Support for toggling IGW-enabled public subnets vs fully private (no IGW) setups
Option to choose centralized NAT (single NAT in a chosen AZ with route-table pointing to it) or per-AZ NAT Gateways
Creates VPC endpoints for S3, ECR (api & docker), STS, CloudWatch Logs when enabled, with appropriate route table associations
Outputs VPC id, subnet ids by type, route table ids, endpoint ids, and tags (map) as strings or list of strings
A post-provision validator run succeeds in a fresh dev account validating: route to internet for public subnets, NAT egress for private subnets, and DNS reachability to endpoints
Module has clear upgrade notes and a documented migration path for changes to default route tables or NAT topology
Unit/integration tests (terratest or kitchen-terraform) exist and run in CI with a smoke plan/apply/validate stage
tasks: Design module inputs/outputs and default variables (CIDR strategy, az_count, subnet_prefixes)
Implement core resources: aws_vpc, aws_subnet (public/private/isolated), aws_internet_gateway, aws_nat_gateway, aws_route_table and aws_route_table_association
Implement VPC endpoints creation logic with a toggle and endpoint policy support
Add tagging and naming conventions consistent with Redwood naming guidelines
Add optional flow logs support and CloudWatch Log group creation option
Create null_resource-based post-provision validator script and integrate into Makefile/CI
Write Terraform docs (README examples: minimal, production, centralized-nat) and upgrade notes
Add terratest/kitchen scenarios and wire them into CI pipeline
Open initial PR and iterate on review feedback
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with infra and private-deploy PMs. Agreed on per-AZ by-default NAT, centralized-NAT as opt-in. (Asha)
2026-02-17: WIP: initial variable schema and README outline pushed to feature branch (feature/vpc-module-initial). See design doc link.
2026-02-20: Prototype creates VPC + subnets + IGW successfully in dev account; added naming/tagging helpers. (Diego)
2026-02-24: Decided to implement endpoint policies as optional JSON variable to support restrictive customer use-cases. (Security review asked for explicit opt-in).
2026-02-27: Added post-provision validator skeleton; validator checks route table default route, NAT egress to 8.8.8.8, and resolves s3.amazonaws.com via VPC endpoint when enabled.
2026-03-01: Pushed tests (terratest) for minimal and centralized-nat scenarios. CI currently running; two failing assertions around route propagation — investigating.
risk_and_mitigation: State drift when switching between centralized and per-AZ NAT: mitigation — provide a documented migration script and recommend terragrunt plan with targeted route_table replacements
Customer CIDR collisions: mitigation — include validation logic to warn if supplied CIDR overlaps with common RFC1918 ranges used by Redwood internal networks and a flag to skip the check
Endpoint policy mishaps could block callers: mitigation — default to allowed minimal policy and require explicit opt-in for restrictive policies; include example policies in docs
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate + fmt + tflint in pre-commit
Integration: terratest scenarios that provision in ephemeral sandbox accounts, run the post-provision validator, and then destroy
CI: add a gated job that runs plan for a mock production workspace and requires manual approval for apply
Upgrade test: create a workspace with v0.1 defaults then run apply against v0.2 to validate state migrations (recorded in upgrade-notes.md)
rollout_plan: Merge to main after PR approvals and green CI
Publish module to internal registry with semantic version v0.2.0
Notify Solutions and Customer Success of breaking changes via release notes
Tag existing Private deployment templates to reference the new module and test a single internal customer in a canary rollout before wider adoption
blockers: Need final approval from Security for default endpoint policies (ticket raised to security team)
CI quota limits in sandbox accounts causing intermittent terratest failures
notes: Keep resource-level timeouts conservative for customers with slow API responses; expose as variables
Prefer aws_eip for NAT gateways to make EIP rotation explicit during upgrades
Avoid assuming number of AZs in account; module will accept azs list or az_count and compute subnets accordingly
